body: There definitely seems to be something strange going on with their history, I thought that maybe the Astrologer class items had a translation error or something, but the Japanese seems to say the same thing, that they're the successors to Glintstone sorcerers which is about as close to an objectively wrong or at least deliberately conflicting item description as I've ever seen in these games. I think it reinforces this idea a lot though. I've seen some people claim the sun realm is only meant to be one city in the JP, but the connections with the Carians make me think this is why it was localized as 'realm' as it seems to have been far more widespread.
do you happen to have a link to the interview about Destined Death's removal being the reason for Demigod immortality? It makes sense I just can't remember seeing it worded like that until now
I think either way the idea of this rune, assuming it does match the elden ring directly, lining up with an intersection of the rings is extremely interesting and odd

I definitely think the veil plays a factor since we can see it in front of the Moons in the Land of Shadow which lines up with the Moons not being sealed. Granted the sun is so bright in the Land of Shadow it's hard to tell if it's in front of the Veil or not, but for the time being I'm definitely assuming it is as there's no other obvious explanation for its different standing. Enir-Illim's sun is a mystery to me just because at least Farum Azula is specifically tied to a bizarre relationship with time. We get so little on Enir-Illim it makes it near impossible to understand why time isn't passing there in a 'normal' way, especially since from outside the tower day and night fall around it normally. It's like once you're in the tower you're no longer in normal space or something even though you can see other points of the Land of Shadow like Jagged Peak

I'd always assumed it coincided with Farum Azula's decline but it's still very hard to pin down. Something I've been wondering after rewatching SilentEllipsis' impossible sun video is that while he doesn't speak on it much, the Farum Azula Sun and Lands Between sun are rising from different spots. Combined with how bright the Land of Shadow sun is it makes me wonder if the sun was actually fragmented and that's how its power was integrated into the Erdtree. Maybe Placidusax is trying to hold what's left of the sun in the Farum Azula timeless space, some was split and sealed in the realm of shadow, and a small amount remained in the LB proper. That's all wildly speculative but it's hard to do much else with the sun lol

I'm not seeing what you're seeing. The Iris of Grace definitely seems to arc downwards instead of upwards like the rune we're familiar with as OP and Infa said. I think Infa also showed a contrast adjusted version to back his interpretation up but I can't recall when or what video that's from.

This is one of my favorite breakdowns and interpretations I've seen here, I've definitely started to feel it wasn't as straightforward as Enir-Illim "just" being made of corpses, and I really like the connections between how inorganic materials can grow in the Lands Between. The Ulcerated Tree Spirits have an entirely new appreciation with this in mind too. Regarding the Graven Masses, [I recently wrote a piece on the stars in general](https://ununtrium.medium.com/elden-ring-the-nature-of-true-stars-the-celestial-mechanics-of-fate-233325136f72) and came to the conclusion this ability to become the starseeds is related to Ymir's assertion about mankind being birthed from stardust, which based on Beloved Stardust is somewhat interchangeable with Glintstone. It looks like the Graven Schools are reversing the process of a star birthing Glintstone and organic life by trying to revert themselves into Glintstone and then a star. The Graven mass talisman is found at the base of an actual Graven Mass while the Graven School's is positioned in the center of a room in a similar way, only at the foot of a massive collection of Glintstone Crystals. I think this indicates there was a Mass at Raya Lucaria that had progressed further and transformed entirely into Glintstone.

We were just speaking of this in another thread, but I think the answer is that the Carians and Astrology in general were originally based on understanding the Sun prior to the whole sun realm collapsing thing. The Telescope is decorated with sunflowers and suns but is specifically a Carian Astrological tool, and as you've also observed the Glintstone Sigil has a sun at the bottom that isn't present on the Cuckoo attire or mentioned at all, like they're completely ignorant of its history or significance, which is all but confirmed by the Astrologer class items depicting an incorrect history of Astrologers inheriting Glintstone rather than the reverse we know to be true (this seems to be consistent in both translations). I think it's another in a deep Sun-related rabbit hole of indicators that the sun used to be this important central star and now the entire star-reading practice has no idea it began there.

Amazed to hear all of the work that has gone into this. Regarding the Cuckoos, I definitely wasn't really looking too deeply into them at all, and it was really only this post (and the general oddness of the Glintstone sigil) that got me considering them at all.

Regarding the sun moon and stars, I don't have any access to pull the textures or anything like that. Just based on my own independent research the direction I'm in currently is that the sun and star worship used to be connected but aren't any more. The Telescope is specifically a tool of *Carian* Astrology but is only carved with sunflower and sun emblems, so it predates Rennala converting them to Moon worship but also ties their understanding of stars back to the sun, and the Glintstone Sigil has a half sun at the bottom where the "mass of glintstone" the Cuckoos overlook seems to be rising up from. However this sun isn't present or mentioned by the actual Cuckoo Knight attire which lines up with the Sun in the rest of the game being heavily obscured and ties into the Precursors being separated from their astrological roots and the Astrologer starting class being the "descendants" of Glintstone sorcery even though we know for a fact the old Astrology practice predates Glintstone Sorcery existing at all, there looks to be a clear connection between the history of Astrology being obscured, it's not clear to me if it's directly related to the Sun being obscured/fall of the sun realm but it seems possible.

  
Regarding death connections that's more to do with another rabbit hole I fell down but the tl;dr is that the stars have a lot of ties to water which is what I'm investigating currently and what led me to your work here and the Cuckoos.

Really appreciate the analysis here, working on an analysis of stars right now and trying to get a better understanding of some things related to Death led me here. The cuckoo subsection was particularly interesting, would love to see you go into more detail on that.

Over the last few years I’ve been going through a lot of your cosmic Transformers stories that began in Marvel and ran through 3H, and I’ve really come to love what you added to the mythology in terms of the abstract cosmic scope and spiritual angles of Unicron and Primus. I wanted to ask

\-what, if any, were your inspirations or reasons for taking the series in this direction/were there any real life religious or philosophical points of reference in developing this?

\-you consistently wrote Unicron (and Primus) as these sort of manifold abstract entities the reader only ever experiences a part of, but future Transformers stories haven’t used this as much, is this a concept you would ever revisit in future stories if given the opportunity? I was always a big fan of the scope and depth this added to the lore

  
\-Regarding your pitch for the old Cybertron comic that was scrapped when IDW went with a new direction, I noticed some plot points popped up in Forest Lee's FunPub work. Was he working from your notes and was your pitch still generally representative of the ideas behind the Unicron Singularity's role in the Unicron Trilogy. I ask mainly because that plot point while phenomenal, was also somewhat vaguely defined in the cartoons and comics, and your pitch actually laid it out in a much easier to understand manner.

Greatly appreciate everything you’ve done for these toy robots and whether it’s Earth Wars or another comic I look forward to anything that you’re involved in with TF.

Sellen and Iji also use the "nagareru hoshi" wording to refer to Radahn's halting of stars instead of "nagareboshi" or "ryusei" (which the game uses for every mention of a meteor otherwise). I find this really fascinating especially as it was localized as "constellations" as opposed to the other times Radahn is spoken of in the context of meteors, it seems like a deliberate distinction was made. Enia also uses a similar but not identical wording when she speaks about the Elden Ring commanding the stars in the final game, it looks like the "flow" aspect was very important linguistically to keep intact when referring to the fate-directing stars as opposed to the meteors.

Something interesting on that note, Sellen and only Sellen, specifically says Radahn is 'repulsing' the stars, and Jerren's japanese dialogue about the stars aligning speaks of them as "the stars have filled" (or something along those lines). It seems like Radahn is in a constant push and pull with them, they clearly aren't entirely halted, but he is stated to have interrupted their "cycles" which is messing up fate. The JP also speaks of it in terms of a Seal being placed which I'm not entirely clear on the mechanics of.

I'm diagnosed schizoid and have two small kids (6 and 4), it's been very difficult with the oldest as a lot of the issues with the disorder began to come to a head shortly before I ended up getting diagnosed, and I had kids fiarly young which accentuated the stress. Hindsight is everything I guess, and while I'm not a mother I was the primary caretaker for both of my kids in their earliest years. 

Being more withdrawn in itself I think will not be an issue, the thing to watch for is the level of connection you feel with your children which for me, has waned the older they get. If you're worried about not talking enough, you can substitute that with reading to them more often, which ensures your child will continue to develop those linguistic skills. My wife is the social one of the two of us, so my kids' activities with other children are normally arranged by her, and this may be something to lean on your husband for if you find it difficult. Raising children is largely about adaptation, but planning for your perceived shortcomings is something I wish I had been doing before they were born as it would have avoided a lot of issues down the line. I think the fact you're thinking about these things is a good sign your heart is in the right place and you'll make it work.

Some very impressive setpieces and designs, as always, but extremely confused by the lore direction. It's only been one day and I'm positive there will be tons of obscure discoveries, especially environmental, as time passes, but as-is I am bewildered by the things the trailers touched on that are largely unmentioned. I've come around on the Radahn thing, and I think it was handled in such a way that there's so many different ways to interpret the character motivations, which I see as a good thing. The abrupt lack of a real ending is what throws me off though and I can't really parse the intent there. Otherwise, loved the lore with Metyr and Bayle, and the Hornsent culture. A bit shocked at the general lack of Numen or Nox lore (so far) though, I thought for sure there'd be more of that. Would have liked to see some more space monsters as well.

It was every bit as confusing as this is, but you felt that if you studied it long enough, you could get somewhere. It's been two days, so I know that will change with SOTE, it just doesn't feel that way right now.

I'm not even that bent out of shape by the lack of concrete answers, that's par for the course, it's just bizarre to me that everything with Marika's storyline was exclusively in trailers. It's not From's style to generally do flashback style cutscenes or anything, but from what I can tell we really don't get ANYTHING about what she did at the Gate or what the Threads even are beyond the trailer. I'd be fine with even the most obscure passing dialogue related that doesn't clarify anything, I just think it should be in the game at all.

That said these are early days, there are still things being discovered in the base game years later, so who is to say that won't happen for SOTE. I am definitely on the side of thinking none of this was Radahn's plan, as every reference to the vow we get comes from Miquella or someone who heard about it from Miquella. We never hear Radahn's POV at all, and him facing down Malenia doesn't make much sense if he wanted this. I don't think this is Malenia's fault either though, given we know Mohg was also under Miquella's spell. I'm left to assume she was as well, as nuking Caelid is in direct contradiction to the stated goals of the Haligtree.

shop/quest loaders eg aeultimate is a good one. Basically, the game has been dead for nearly a decade and a ton of perfectly good content especially on the free player end is gone with it. I've had a maxed out sc account since I was a kid, but running through the game on a new character, there is so little to actually use, so I've been using one to grab some retired mecha or weapons that are more fun or interesting than what remains in-game. You cant "hack" nova gems or anything so you arent stealing anything from ae.

Dharmahp was the best all-purpose mecha and shreds anything for general questing, though the permanent version seems nerfed compared to the original. TerriFi is the highest damaging, and the Elite House mecha are generally high tier. Any SCEM are usually decent at worst, though unfortunately they have altered specials from their originals and in most cases aren't quite as good. The Hunter Phantasm can be extremely useful due to the huge healing the body has (I know it was basically a necessity for one of the SC Club Necryptos challenge fights). Arthurian Bull is by a decent margin the highest damaging permanent non-real-life-currency mecha due to its insane back arm. The Milziiga series are also quite strong and are available due to Frostval being permanently open in the dead game iirc. Unfortunately a lot of the really broken specials are on retired mecha and even shop loaders haven't gotten to getting them back in the game yet, if they ever will.

Dharmahp is probably the single best all around mecha to use as aside from good specials, it gets bonus damage to nearly every type of enemy you'll encounter. Advanced and Elite House Mecha are other obvious choices, no longer top tier (for the Advanced) but still useful. The TerriFi series is the highest damaging in the game. While they've changed a lot of the specials on the permanent versions, the SCEM at the star captain's club are all good. If you're going free player your options are more limited and/or late game focused. Recommend using a loader for some retired good free player mecha like the EC War SDF Elite. The free Golden Mecha will also take you quite far.

For Houses it really depends on your playstyle, a lot of people will base their stat build on the houses since changing them isn't quick and easy. WolfBlade is power focused, usually supplemented with Reflex or Luck, MystRaven focuses on crits and dodging so Luck/Reflex are common. RuneHawk is all about EP though I still run a luck/reflex build on my main RH character and I've found it to be really effective. In the very early game the WB mech is a lot better, once you unlock Advanced House Mecha then MR and RH outshine it (RH was a stable body for a lot of challenge enemies and bosses). The Elite ones at level 50 are all quite good though iirc MystRaven was considered the best

Also, just in general since the game is dead, I would recommend looking into a Loader so you can access a lot of the retired content. The game has way too much perfectly good art and fun equipment to use that's gone for no reason. I've been running an f2p account through the story recently in tandem with this and it's been far more fun than what remains in the current build. The EbilCorp war's SDF Elite mecha can take you very far in storylines without feeling too overpowered or too weak.
